text:
Predicates:
Costs(x, y) ::: It costs y dollars to take the GRE test.
Provides(x, y, z) ::: x provides financial aid to y who prove z.
Hardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
SingleParent(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
OutOfWork(x, y) ::: x has been out of work for more than y years.
ApplyFor(x, y, z) ::: x can apply for financial aid from y to take the GRE test.
Premises:
Costs(GRE, 205) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x (Provides(ETS, x, Hardship(x))) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
Hardship(economicHardship) ↔ (LittleMoney(economicHardship) ∨ FewResources(economicHardship)) ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
SingleParent(tom) ∧ OutOfWork(dad, 1) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family. His dad has been out of work for more than a year.
Conclusion:
ApplyFor(tom, ETS, economicHardship) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
